title: Draup Sales Prompt Library
tagline: Ready-to-use prompts for Claude, ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot that turn Draup's sales intelligence into account briefs, buyer maps, target lists and outreach.

categories.name: Start here
categories.desc: Tell your AI who you are and what you sell, once. Every other prompt gets sharper.

categories.name: Account research

categories.name: Buyers and stakeholders

categories.name: Tech stack and displacement

categories.name: Signals and timing

categories.name: Outreach and messaging

categories.name: Prospecting and target lists

categories.name: Solution plays: by what you sell

categories.name: Deal strategy and qualification
categories.desc: Win live opportunities: re-engage stalled deals, answer RFPs, build business cases, handle objections and beat a named competitor.

categories.name: Competitive intelligence

categories.name: Outsourcing and services deals
categories.desc: For IT services, consulting and staffing sellers: incumbents, share of wallet, GCCs and wedges.

categories.name: Account planning and expansion

categories.name: Expansion and cross-sell

categories.name: Partners and alliances

categories.name: Industry and market intelligence

categories.name: Sales leadership and RevOps

SDR.name: SDR / BDR
SDR.desc: Find who to contact and why now, then write outreach that references real facts.

AM.name: Account & Customer Success Manager
AM.desc: Grow and protect existing accounts: risk checks, expansion, QBRs.

LEAD.name: Sales Leader & RevOps
LEAD.desc: Size markets, tier accounts, carve territories and focus the team.

MKT.name: Marketing & ABM
MKT.desc: Pick target accounts and write messages tied to what each account is doing.

SE.name: Presales & Solutions
SE.desc: Understand architecture, priorities and incumbents before the technical conversation.

SVC.name: Services, SI & Staffing Seller
SVC.desc: Map outsourcing incumbents, share of wallet, GCCs and displacement wedges.

PTN.name: Partnerships & Alliances
PTN.desc: Find co-sell partners already embedded in your target accounts.

fin.name: Company & financials
fin.desc: Profile, revenue, EBITDA, IT and R&D spend, forecasts, revenue by business unit and region, IT spend split, private funding.

calls.name: Earnings calls & filings
calls.desc: Earnings-call and press-call transcripts with speakers, plus annual filings for US-listed companies.

pri.name: Priorities & opportunities
pri.desc: Stated initiatives from earnings calls and news, by function and workload, with the tech and service providers attached; Draup-generated entry points.

exe.name: Executives & movement
exe.desc: Key executives with level, budget control, workloads, past companies and LinkedIn; recent hires, promotions and exits.

tech.name: Tech stack
tech.desc: Products in use with last-seen dates and usage strength, vendor landscape per workload, products adopted in the last 12 months.

hire.name: Hiring & job postings
hire.desc: Posting volume and monthly trend, skills trending up or down, full job descriptions, market-wide 'who is hiring for X'.

flow.name: Talent flow & locations
flow.desc: Hiring, attrition and net change by month, company and metro; key locations with HQ, GCC and new-site flags.

sig.name: News signals
sig.desc: Account and market news by category: M&A, layoffs, funding, expansion, executive moves, partnerships, product launches.

out.name: Outsourcing deals
out.desc: Customer-to-provider engagements: who outsources which workloads to whom, relationship tier, delivery locations.

eco.name: Industry ecosystem
eco.desc: Industry revenue, IT and R&D spend, priorities, fast-growing tech, top vendors and outsourcers, growing and shrinking companies, startups, talent hubs.

uni.name: Company directory
uni.desc: List building and market sizing by industry, HQ, size, technology, service providers and outsourced workloads.

tal.name: Talent cost & supply
tal.desc: Base pay by role and city, talent pool size and growth, hiring difficulty, layoffs, employer brand (Draup for Talent connector).

trust_notes: Numbers: IT spend is a Draup estimate, often modelled from revenue, so use it for scale, not as a signal. Industry totals are global. Financials are in the company's reporting currency and fiscal year.
Freshness: news and hiring update continuously; leadership moves can lag by about three months, and brand-new executives may not appear yet.
People: some senior leaders have no function tag, so the prompts widen to C-level titles when needed. Draup can't search people by name.
Outsourcing engagements are Draup-derived records of work between a company and its providers, not published contracts.
Every drafted email ends with a "Check before sending" line listing any single-source or conflicting facts. Competitor tools are rated Red, Amber or Green by how entrenched they are.
Give the website the company actually uses (some parents use domains like home.barclays), and check names, titles and numbers before anything goes to a customer.
